You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Cmc2₁ (No. 36, Hall symbol C 2c -2), but the supplied input cell is not the conventional C-centered orthorhombic cell. The input lattice is a hexagonal-appearing primitive cell with a = b = 13.46326204 Å, c = 7.340415 Å, α = β = 90°, and γ = 161.22719459°, containing 20 atoms with the declared composition Ho₄Sn₁₀Rh₆. All atomic positions are given as fractional coordinates, and the input and standard frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0) and the matrix P has rows (0.5, 0.5, 0), (−0.5, 0.5, 0), and (0, 0, 1) to within the stated floating-point precision. Thus the standard orthorhombic a axis is the sum of the input a and b vectors, the standard b axis is their difference, and the c axis is unchanged; no origin translation is applied. Input fractional coordinates are rounded to six decimal places, and no positional corrections beyond this rounding are required.

In the standard Cmc2₁ setting, all atoms occupy the same Wyckoff orbit type 4a, with the coordinate relation (0, y, z); the C-centering and the polar c-glide generate the full set of four equivalent positions from each representative. Because every independent atom lies on the mirror plane x = 0, the structure is fully specified by ten independent (y, z) pairs, and the multiplicities sum to the 40 atoms of the conventional C-centered cell, corresponding to the 20 atoms of the primitive input cell.

The two inequivalent holmium sublattices both lie on 4a sites. The first Ho orbit has its representative at (0, 0.172638, 0.244554), and the second Ho orbit at (0, 0.475936, 0.263843); each has multiplicity four. Tin occupies five independent 4a orbits. Their representatives are (0, 0.119411, 0.768989) for the first Sn site, (0, 0.295333, 0.450307) for the second, (0, 0.403634, 0.885889) for the third, (0, 0.047589, 0.102326) for the fourth, and (0, 0.290525, 0.021970) for the fifth, each again of multiplicity four. Rhodium occupies three independent 4a orbits, with representatives at (0, 0.050150, 0.481254), (0, 0.223382, 0.734794), and (0, 0.394015, 0.518074), each with multiplicity four.

Taken together, the ten symmetry-independent atoms on the x = 0 mirror plane, replicated by the Cmc2₁ symmetry operations and transformed back to the input cell through the inverse of the given change-of-frame matrix, reproduce the complete Ho₄Sn₁₀Rh₆ structure in the original 13.46326204 Å × 13.46326204 Å × 7.340415 Å cell with γ = 161.22719459°.
